Marissa / team — draft of technical answers below (happy to shorten for customer-facing response).

What we log (high level):
- Admin actions: user creation/deletion, role/permission changes, privilege grants and revocations, password/KMS key operations (metadata only), session starts/stops.
- Console auth events: successful/failed sign-ins, MFA challenges, IP/geo metadata.
- Operator actions: deploy/rollback events, model version pins, config changes to routing/policy, autoscale events.
- API/service calls that impact tenant state: API key creation/revocation, token issuance (metadata only).
- System telemetry: process restarts, host-level events (for forensic tie-in).

Retention:
- Default: 90 days (hot index).
- Extended: we can provide 12-month and 24-month export packages on request (requires 7–10 business days to assemble and verify).
- For SOC 2 evidence we typically provide a 12-month snapshot unless the customer requests a full 24-mo handoff.

Export formats & packaging:
- NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) is primary; can also export CSV or syslog-style text for SIEM ingest.
- Each export bundle includes: data files, a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums), a delivery audit.txt (timestamped inventory), and an HMAC signature file for attestation.
- Sample manifest and a 2-line syslog snippet attached (sample_export_manifest.csv, syslog-snippet.txt).

Transport options:
- Option A (preferred for large / automated pulls): push to customer's S3 bucket via presigned PUT URL, with server-side encryption required.
- Option B (common): SFTP push to customer-managed endpoint; we provide PGP-encrypted tarball.
- Option C (ad-hoc): password-protected Drive share with PGP encrypted payload (least preferred for chain-of-custody).

Chain-of-custody & verification:
- We provide signed manifest + delivery receipt. For higher assurance we can include notarized timestamp via third-party timestamping service.

Notes: cannot include raw message body contents that contain PII in exported admin logs by default — only metadata and identifiers. Redaction rules: we can mask email addresses and replace user IDs with stable hashed identifiers on request.

Ben
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sample_export_manifest.csv, syslog-snippet.txt

Ben — this is a good technical summary. A few compliance/operational points to call out before we send to BlueWave:

- Redaction & PII: per our policy, admin logs contain identifiers (user_id, username, IP) but not plaintext customer payloads. We will apply a standardized redaction template for any field flagged as PII. On the audit_request_form we'll mark what will be redacted and what will be pseudonymized (stable hash).
- Legal sign-off: small clause requested for delivery: "Delivery constitutes a one-time attested snapshot for audit purposes; Redwood retains discretion over operational logs and requires a signed evidence transfer addendum for recurring deliveries." I can draft the addendum if they need recurring exports.
- Sampling: if BlueWave only needs a subset (e.g., a canary week or quarter sample), recommend a rolling 7-day or 30-day sample window for quicker turnaround.
- Timeline: 7 business days for a one-off 12-month bundle is reasonable. If they request chain-of-custody notarization add 3 business days.

I'll join any customer call to confirm redaction choices. Sharing a short readout doc here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example

Kimberly Park
